cohort: All births in British Columbia, Canada between 2008 and 2018 with a family physician, obstetrician, or midwife as the most responsible provider (n = 425,056)
finding: Midwifery clients consistently had lower adjusted absolute and relative risks of adverse neonatal outcomes across all medical risk strata compared to those with physicians as their most responsible provider.
mod_finding: Midwifery clients experienced higher rates of spontaneous vaginal births, vaginal births after cesarean delivery and breastfeeding initiation, and lower rates of cesarean deliveries and instrumental births, with no increase in adverse neonatal outcomes; however, there was an increased risk of oxytocin induction among high-risk birthers with a midwife versus an obstetrician.
